TM Vibrant Shaders.name: TM Vibrant Shaders
TM Vibrant Shaders.author: cheatoskar
TM Vibrant Shaders.description: Real-time lighting and weather mod for TrackMania Nations/United Forever and TrackMania 2. Features include dynamic lighting, night mode, long shadows, neon effects, rain, clouds, improved water, MP4 video export, and customizable hotkeys. Open the menu with F8.

1.4.0-rc.2.changelog:
TM Vibrant Shaders 1.4.0:

Real-time lighting, weather and skies for TrackMania Nations & United Forever and TrackMania 2 (ManiaPlanet 4). This release replaces 1.4.0-preview.

New: TrackMania 2 (ManiaPlanet 4) Support:

TM Vibrant Shaders now runs in ManiaPlanet 4: TrackMania² Stadium, Canyon, Valley and Lagoon, natively on the game's Direct3D 11 renderer (tested in the game on Stadium). It provides the same mod experience with the same F8 menu, presets and settings as in Nations and United Forever, built on what ManiaPlanet's engine knows: surface normals, material colours, sun shadow maps, motion vectors and HDR image.

TrackMania 2 Stadium, photo mode's compare split: left the game as it is, right with the mod (black hole sky).

What it does in TrackMania 2:
- Skies: Clear sky, starry night, black hole, aurora, ring world, with the map darkened to a real night beneath them (Real night): the engine's sky light comes down to moonlight, lamps and neon stay lit.
- Light: Ambient occlusion and contact shadows, bounce light (GI) and neon light on the surroundings, from the engine's own normals. Lamps, light strips, screens and halos glow as the engine draws them (Game light sources).
- Soft sun shadows (on, 1°): sharp where a thing touches the ground, softer the farther they fall. Nothing in the game's memory changes; whether ManiaPlanet's anti-cheat minds the replaced shadow shader is not known (0 turns it off).
- Atmosphere: Haze and fog, light shafts, volumetric light through the engine's shadow maps, volumetric clouds, lens flare.
- Weather: Rain, snow, wet roads, puddles with reflections, lightning, drops on the lens, rain and howling storm sound.
- Cinema: Depth of field, motion blur and TAA with the engine's motion vectors; photo mode (F6) with the compare split (Shift+F6), also against a preset.
- Neon trail following the car's real position in the engine.
- Author's Shader: Looks stored in a map's comments are applied when the map loads; Set as Author's Shader works in the map editor.
- The interface stays sharp: the mod draws before the HUD and its tone map replaces the engine's.

Install (TrackMania 2 / ManiaPlanet 4):
1. Download TM-Vibrant-Shaders.zip (one zip for both games) and extract it.
2. Close ManiaPlanet and run TM-Vibrant-Shaders-Setup.exe.
3. Start ManiaPlanet 64-bit. F8 opens the menu, F5 switches effects on/off (F7 is ManiaPlanet's friends list).

Highlights for TrackMania Nations Forever & United Forever:

New F8 Menu:
- Every preset as an interactive card with a picture, brief description, and GPU load.
- Point at a preset for a live preview; click to apply; right-click to assign per map mood (Day, Sunset, Night).
- Dedicated pages for Customize, Studio (all settings), Maps (Author's Shader & mood defaults), and Performance.
- Save custom presets with live in-game thumbnails, or share a look as one line of text (Copy share code / Paste share code, works between both games).
- Hotkeys can be changed; Reload shaders moved to Ctrl+F9, so the mod works next to the 100% TMX + Bingo mod.

Light from the game itself:
- Game HDR and Game light sources (on by default): lamps, floodlights, start lights and neon borders glow as the game draws them, nothing is guessed from bright pixels. Floodlit white stays even at night, grass and car paint no longer glow.
- Long mesh shadows from the game's own meshes, from the sun or the black hole; fences and grids cast their lattice.
- Real night under night skies (on by default): day and sunset maps under night skies are lit at midnight by the engine itself (moonlight and lamps, no baked sun); under the black hole the game's moon shines from it.

Photo Mode (F6, automatic with free camera cam 7):
- Full quality with extended draw distance: ambient occlusion, reflections, shadows, and bounce light reach 3x as far (long shadows cover 960m).
- Compare split (Shift+F6): the vanilla look or any preset on the other side of a movable line (Ctrl+Shift+Wheel), with both names in the photos.
- Works even with shaders off (F7): aperture / depth of field and CAS sharpening on the vanilla game look, with autofocus on the car.
- F12 saves photos without HUD; Shift+F12 saves high-resolution tiled photos.

Performance and video:
- Render scale with AMD FSR 1 (off by default): the game and the effects at a fraction of the screen's resolution, scaled up before the HUD; at 0.67 the effects cost about half.
- MP4 video export: the replay editor's Shoot video writes H.264 or HEVC with AAC sound, encoded by the graphics card, with the effects at full quality on the video's own clock.
- Auto quality measures every effect on your GPU and turns off just enough of them, never the long shadows, the light shafts or the neon light.

Neon Trail & Audio:
- The neon trail tracks the car's true position directly from the engine: no flicker, no gaps, along banked roads and loops; earlier runs can stay, dimmer.
- Realistic storm audio: recorded winter storm wind for snowstorms.

Known issues:
- Night presets: some blue printed signs (the blue "d" of the Trackmania United banner) glow like neon strips; the game draws them with the same material as the strips.

Install (TrackMania Nations Forever / United Forever):
1. Download TM-Vibrant-Shaders.zip and extract it.
2. Run TM-Vibrant-Shaders-Setup.exe to install into TrackMania ModLoader or game folders.
3. In-game: F8 opens menu, F7 toggles shaders.

Full details in the changelog.

1.4.1.changelog:
The first release for TrackMania 2 (ManiaPlanet 4) as well, with a new menu and the game's own light. It follows 1.4.0-preview (2026-10-12) and its release candidates (there is no plain 1.4.0); this list covers everything since 1.3.0.

New:
- TrackMania 2 (ManiaPlanet 4) support (see the end of this list). One zip and one setup for both games.
- New F8 menu: every preset as a card with a picture, a line about it and its GPU load. Point at one and the game shows it, click to use it, right click to use it on day, sunset or night maps. Pages Shaders, Customize (the everyday settings), Studio (every setting), Maps, Performance, Settings and About. Short labels with the details in tooltips, the mod's icon in the header, sized for the screen. Your own presets get a picture of the game when you save them.
- Menu: Studio's settings sorted into clearer groups (Image split into Image quality and Game integration, the latter last; Haze and light shafts out of Sky), the main sliders first in each group; Customize gets a Colour panel and the same order as Studio; every setting has a tooltip.
- Share a look as text: Copy share code / Paste share code on the Shaders page put a look on the clipboard as one line (TMVS1:...) for a chat. The same code works in TrackMania Nations/United and TrackMania 2.
- Hotkeys can be changed (Settings page, Hotkeys). Reload shaders is now Ctrl+F9, so the mod works next to the 100% TMX + Bingo mod: the menu under the pointer gets the mouse.
- Photo mode (F6, on by itself with the free camera): no HUD, full quality, effects reach three times as far. F12 saves a photo without the HUD, Shift+F12 a hi-res photo; middle click sets the focus, Shift+wheel zooms. Works with the effects switched off too.
- Compare split (Shift+F6): the game's image or any preset on the other side of a line, on the same frame and in photos, with both names at the line.
- Light from the game itself: Game HDR gives the mod the game's image with light brighter than white, and Game light sources makes lamps, floodlights, start lights and neon borders glow as the game draws them instead of guessing lamps from bright pixels: no more glowing grass, banners or car paint at night. Neon strip glow, Floodlights, Lamp glare and Lamp haze glow tune them.
- Real night under night skies (Real night): with a night sky or the black hole over a day or sunset map, the game lights the map at midnight itself (its moon, no baked sun). The map, its replays and validation stay as they are. Game moonlight lets the game's moon shine from the black hole, or turns it off.
- Long mesh shadows: long shadows from the game's own meshes, from the sun or the black hole, without popping; with Fence shadows fences and grids cast their lattice.
- Render scale with AMD FSR 1 (Image quality, off by default): the game and the effects at a fraction of the screen's resolution, scaled up before the HUD, which stays sharp. At 0.67 the effects cost about half.
- MP4 video export: Shoot video in the replay editor writes an MP4 (H.264 or HEVC, sound as AAC), encoded by the graphics card, no codec dialog. The effects run on the video's own clock at full quality, also with the export's supersampling.
- Colour looks from .cube files (Studio, Colour look (LUT)) on top of every preset.
- Focus on the car: Focus on -> Car keeps your car sharp in replays and photo mode.
- Neon trail from the car's real position in the game: no flicker at speed, no gaps, it lies along banked roads, walls and loops and keeps going through the map's clips. Earlier runs kept shows the last runs, dimmer.
- Rain and snow stay outside: nothing falls under roofs, bridges and in buildings, and the lens dries off under a wide roof.
- Update check: the menu says when a new release is out (nothing is downloaded; it can be switched off).
- ModLoader update server: with one line in the ModLoader's config.yaml the ModLoader installs the mod and every new version itself (install). The About page tells ModLoader users about it.
- The snowstorm's wind is a real recording.
- New settings Haze distance, Highlight roll-off, Floodlit surfaces and Game sunset clouds.
- Experimental, off: Game normals (the game's own shaders hand the mod their normals). Night on game light (their light) is not in the menu: GameLight=1 in settings.ini.
- tmvs.log writes a performance line every 2000 frames (performance).
- SMAA edge smoothing (Image quality, SMAA instead of FXAA, on in every preset but Performance): smoother long edges and sharper textures than FXAA for about 0.2 ms more at 1440p. Older settings.ini and preset files keep FXAA.

Changed defaults:
- On: Game HDR, Game light sources, Clean highlights, Long mesh shadows, Fence shadows, Gap-free long shadows, Clean water, Replay menu shading, Real night, Game moonlight from the black hole, Turn off game FX (the game's own bloom and colour filter, from the next map on), temporal AA (not in Performance) with TAA jitter, MP4 for the video export and Best export quality.
- Lamp glare 0.7 and Lamp haze glow 1. The night presets (Neon, Horizon, Aurora): neon borders glow at 3, the dry track has a sheen instead of a mirror. Neon's bounce light 1, Horizon's bloom 0.15, more neon light spill on Vibrant, Realistic, Competition and Performance. Snowstorm: no snow on the ground, thicker haze.
- Horizon: sky rotation 0, planet direction 20°, Night darkening 0.5 (was automatic). The Ring world sky darkens the night by 0.5; its On the rings view places the planet and the black hole for that view (black hole size 4.5 at 25° height, planet size 1.15 at 20° and -4°, sky rotation 150).
- Sharpening 0.8 (was 0.35; Competition 0.8, was 0.5). Share codes made with an earlier version keep their sharpening.
- Picked preset applies to all maps of this type is off: a preset you pick holds on every map until you choose presets per map type again on the Maps page.

1.4.2.changelog:
A new video export, resource packs, the Horror look with car headlights, clear water and splashes, a fix for overlapped blocks, photo mode in the MediaTracker, and the Misc page (TrackMania Nations/United); car spray, menu windows, the Horror look and car headlights also in TrackMania 2.

New:
- Photo mode in the replay editor's MediaTracker (TrackMania Nations/United): the focus click lands where you click in the small 3D view (it was mapped to the whole screen), the screenshot of an F12 capture is of the view only, and clicks on the editor's panels stay the game's.
- Photo panel: with the effects off its look sliders are greyed (photo mode shows the game's own image then) with a Turn on button; Hide car switches the car's shadow off with the game's own item setters. The exposure, vignette and grain sliders make the preset Custom like the menu's (the replay editor's changing light put the preset's values back over them). Hide car also hides the car's shadow; Hide editor no longer waits for the game to call its interface switch.
- Hide editor in photo mode (Hide editor, off; TrackMania Nations/United): the replay editor's panels hidden with the game's own interface switch (its Tab key), the 3D view filling the screen.
- A compact photo panel (TrackMania Nations/United; exposure, aperture, zoom, vignette, grain, focus, hide car / HUD), Ctrl+F6 hides it for a clean view.
- Hide car in photo mode (Hide car, off; TrackMania Nations/United): the cars (body, glass, lights) are left out of the picture and the photos.
- Pages in windows: every menu page (Shaders, Customize, Studio, Maps, Performance, Video, Resource packs, Settings, About) can be popped out into a window of its own with the symbol on its tab. Move, resize, minimize or close it (the page goes back to the tab bar), keep it on screen over the game when the menu is closed, set its opacity. Places and states are saved and come back after a restart ([Windows] in settings.ini). Also in the TrackMania 2 build.
- Headlight range and beam (Headlight range, 90 m; Headlight beam, 0.5; shown with Car headlights): how far the light reaches (it fades with distance, inverse square, and ends smoothly) and how strongly the cone shows in the air. The lamps sit a little closer to the car and the cone is wider (54 degrees); the glare on a lamp shrinks and fades with distance, so a car far away is a small point, not a searchlight. Horror has thicker haze (5).
- Misc page (TrackMania Nations/United): a minimap in the replay editor and exported videos only, never while you drive (TMX allows no minimap in the race) (the track's shape from the map's blocks and your car; with Real look the blocks as the game draws them, seen from above in their own colours, filling in as the camera sees them; Auto zoom follows the car, 150 m across standing still, 600 m at 500 km/h, never wider than the track, a small track shown whole, held at the finish and gliding back for the next run; the log says what the minimap costs; checkpoints and other special blocks look like plain road), split times at each checkpoint, time and speed, against the map's record from TMX (fetched by itself once per map and kept), the ghost you race against, your best run or a replay file, kept until you restart, with a sector clock, in a window of one height with five checkpoint rows that scroll, each sector after the finish against your best and the reference, and a Session panel (attempts, best / median / last with a graph, respawns, spread, your theoretical best from all your runs and replays of the map, kept per map, the best combined with the reference, the last run sector by sector), and finish effects (confetti, fireworks for a new best run). All off until switched on; the panels sit at the top right and move together; drag a panel away to detach it; everything scales with the game window; the panels are never in photos, the video export or captures. After the game starts a badge at the top centre shows the logo, the mod's version and the keys for the menu and the effects for 10 seconds.
- Horror preset and car headlights (Car headlights, 0; Horror sets 1): the Horror look is a black night with every lamp and neon strip off (floodlights, glows, spill and neon at 0, light intensity 0, the night darkens what the game baked at full), thick fog, and two spotlights from the front of your car as the only light: they light the road and walls ahead, show as beams in the fog and glare when the camera looks into them. No shadows from the headlights. Works with any preset through the setting.
- Horror and car headlights in TrackMania 2 (Car headlights, Headlight range, Headlight beam): the two spotlights on the car the camera follows (read from the constants the game draws it with, as for the spray), lighting the game's own material colours, normals and shine, with beams in the haze and glare. Which way the car faces comes from its motion, until then from the chase camera. Floodlights there turns every light the game draws as light down or off (lamps, neon, screens); at 0 under a night sky, as in Horror, the lamps' light in the light maps and the moon go too, also on night maps.
- Resource packs, Apply on the card: the chosen card gets a small Apply button when the loaded map shows something else, so you don't scroll up to Apply now; the card says how it went. None shows the Realistic preset's picture (the game's own look).

1.4.3-rc.1.changelog:
TM Vibrant Shaders 1.4.3 (pre-release):

Fixes for TrackMania Nations & United Forever, and the mod now works next to the VR mod TrackMania Forever OpenXR. TrackMania 2 is unchanged.

Tell me what breaks (with Documents\TrackMania\TMVS\tmvs.log).

Fixed:

- Dirt no longer mirrors walls after you were in the replay editor (also online): the mod kept the old materials' kinds for new ones the game put at the same place in memory.
- Your car stays smooth with TAA, driving and standing still. It used to look grainy while driving, more so with Sharpening.
- No foam on the water above a sunken car.
- The effects run on maps where F7 changed nothing (a TMUnlimiter map of mine set no camera view of its own). On such maps the image also shook; it doesn't any more.
- When the effects are on but nothing is shaded for 2 seconds, tmvs.log now says why.
- Opening the menu (F8) right after the game started could close it (in the first 10 seconds, while the version badge shows). Competition Patch works, 1.5.3 and 2.0.
- When another mod keeps this one from starting (no menu, no effects), tmvs.log now says so after 30 seconds and lists the other mods in the game.

VR (experimental):

With the VR mod TrackMania Forever OpenXR both mods now run together (both from the ModLoader). The mod's menu (F8) shows in the headset. Effects in VR (page Misc & VR, off; restart the game after switching it) shades both eyes, with Comfort, Quality in VR, TAA in VR and Rain on the windshield. Both eyes get the same exposure, sky and rain; without TAA in VR the eyes are shaded without a history over frames, which stopped lamps and the Rain sky from flickering in an earlier test build. Objects at the edge of the view that vanish for a moment (lamps, half a grandstand, the sky going black) come from the VR mod and happen without this mod too (wial663's test). Until it is fixed there, raising Near clip in the VR mod's settings (F10) to about 0.2 m stops it, but then the other cars can lose their roofs; try values in between. Anything else that flickers: tell me, with tmvs.log (it now says every 10 s what was shaded in the headset).

This needs a VR mod build that hands its device to this mod. That change is a pull request to the VR mod; until it is merged, use the build from my fork. The hand-over is by @wial663, who also tested it in the headset. Thanks!

Install (Nations & United Forever):

With the ModLoader, updates itself: close the ModLoader, open %LOCALAPPDATA%\TMLoader\config.yaml with Notepad and add this line under servers::

yaml
  - 'https://cheatoskar.github.io/TM-Vibrant-Shaders/modloader/'

Then tick TM Vibrant Shaders in your profile. New versions arrive on their own from then on. This is a pre-release: that server keeps 1.4.2. To get the pre-releases through the ModLoader, use https://cheatoskar.github.io/TM-Vibrant-Shaders/modloader/beta/ instead.

With the setup: download TM-Vibrant-Shaders.zip, extract it and run TM-Vibrant-Shaders-Setup.exe.

In the game F8 opens the menu and F7 turns the effects on and off. Step by step: installation guide (Deutsch). TrackMania 2 players: the same zip, see 1.4.1's notes.

All changes: changelog.

Release notes: https://github.com/cheatoskar/TM-Vibrant-Shaders/releases/tag/v1.4.3-rc.1

1.6.0.changelog:
One release, two forms from the same code: the standalone mod 1.6.0 for six games (TrackMania Nations Forever, United Forever, Nations ESWC, Sunrise, Original and TrackMania 2), and the same features as four Horizon Client modules 2.0.0 for the five Direct3D 9 games. TrackMania 2 stays standalone: Horizon runs only in the 32-bit Direct3D 9 games. Which game has what: the compatibility table in the README.

1.6.0 (standalone):

The older games: TrackMania Sunrise and TrackMania Original, clips and the MP4 export on all three 2006-engine games.

New (TrackMania Sunrise, TrackMania Original):
- TrackMania Sunrise and TrackMania Original (experimental): the same DLL as d3d9.dll, for the Windows 10 community repack of Sunrise (TmSunrise.exe) and the Online Patch v2 of Original (TMORIGINAL.EXE), each told by its SHA-256. Everything TrackMania Nations ESWC has: the look, photo mode, F12 captures, the car and the race (neon trail, headlights, spray, long mesh shadows, Hide car, split times, the Session panel, finish effects), clips and the MP4 export. The engine is ESWC's generation; its hooks and reads were ported from ESWC (other addresses, a smaller race and player info, no race counters: a start and a respawn are read from your player's info). Not yet: water, the game's materials and light, the minimap (1.7, after a census run in each game). Details in docs/install.md.
- The game's own d3d9.dll stays in use (dgVoodoo in Original, the repack's proxy in Sunrise): the setup renames it to d3d9.chain.dll and the mod passes Direct3D on to it; without one, Windows' own. The uninstall puts it back. tmvs-*.log says which one runs (d3d9: ...).
- Other builds are refused cleanly: an unknown TmSunrise.exe or TMORIGINAL.EXE gets no hook at all, the mod only passes Direct3D on and the log says why (passive: ...).

New (all three older games):
- The game's video export is known: the replay's Shoot video is read from the game (its settings, the frames being written, the game's fixed clock). Best export quality works there: full quality, no auto quality, TAA off when the game supersamples, rain, clouds and the other effects on the video's clock; the clips pause meanwhile.
- MP4 export: the game's AVI writer is hooked as on Forever, so Shoot video writes an MP4 with the mod's encoder (Video format on the Video page: H.264, HEVC or AV1, or the game's AVI), without the codec dialog. Its sound is the game's own, taken with WASAPI process loopback while the game's sound pass runs (the game itself records the default recording device, often a microphone). The game's frames go in, so the settings that need the mod's own frames (HDR blend, HDR10, shutter, lens depth of field, grain) are not shown there (docs/engine-video-export.md).
- Census mode for the materials and light work in 1.7 (development, off by default: LegacyCensus=1 under [dev] in Documents\TrackMania\TMVS\dev.ini): logs once per map each shader the game draws with (class, file, textures), the classes of its per-pass shading, and what the map object offers (blocks, their infos, the coordinates), also when an editor opens. Without the key neither draw hook is installed; in Nations/United Forever the key is ignored.

New (TrackMania Nations ESWC):
- Clips. The Clips page, F4, Ctrl+F4 and Ctrl+Shift+F4 and Save on finish now work on TrackMania Nations ESWC (1.80 patch), and on Sunrise and Original. The race (start, finish, race time), the map's name and its author time are read from the game's own objects, the same reads as the split times; nothing is hooked or written for it. These maps have no UID: the personal best of a clip is kept by the map's name. Details in docs/clips.md.

Changed (TrackMania Nations ESWC):
- Hide car in photo mode now leaves the cars alone in network races (it writes the game's visible bit, so only in solo races and replays). The engine code for ESWC is now the shared one of the three older games; the log lines are the same.

Fixed (all three older games):
- Crash at start when the mod's DLL was loaded at another address than usual: the older games' exes have no import name table, and the mod read the addresses of the imported functions as names. It now finds Direct3DCreate9 by its address.
- Low frame rate in Sunrise with the shaders on (about 15 FPS at 1440p, Upscaling slower than without): Sunrise renders a second, small view into a texture every frame (512x512 with a depth buffer of its own, before the main camera). The mod took it for a second main camera, shaded it and made all its render targets again twice a frame. Such views are now left as the game draws them, and on the older games a camera smaller than the main camera of the last frames never resizes the effects. Temporal effects (TAA, motion blur, exposure) were paused there for the same reason and run again. tmvs.log names the view once (scene: a camera into 512x512 ... is a view into a texture).

Changed (clips, every game):
- Instant replay is off for new players: the clips' background recording (the buffer behind F3, Save last run and the saved best runs) starts only once you switch on Instant replay at the top of the Clips page; then Save best runs is on. Off, nothing is copied or read back from the graphics card, and the clip keys only show "Instant replay is off". A clips.ini that already has it on keeps it. The replay editor's Shoot video doesn't need it.

1.6.1.changelog:
The standalone mod 1.6.1 and the Horizon modules 2.0.1 (the 1.6.1 core).

Changed:
- The perf line in tmvs.log shows where the CPU's time goes: the game's logic between frames, its rendering, the mod's own time (and the part of it blocked waiting for the GPU), the frame end with Present and the game's wait for the GPU, and the frame start, next to the GPU times; plus the game's Cpu/Gpu synchro setting. Details in docs/performance.md.
- The game's Cpu/Gpu synchro is logged (perf: the game's Cpu/Gpu synchro is ...). All five Direct3D 9 games default to Immediate: after every frame the CPU waits until the GPU has finished it, so the GPU time of the effects adds to the frame time in full. 1 Frame or Half a frame in the game's launcher lets the two overlap (docs/performance.md).

Fixed:
- Photo mode no longer switches itself on online: on a server the game puts you into the free camera at the end of every round (and while spectating), and Auto photo mode turned photo mode on each time. It now follows the free camera only offline: the replay editor, a solo race (also the map editor's test drive) and a replay watched from the menu. The mod tells by the class of the race the game runs (a network race, the same signal Horizon Host's "online" uses), also through the second between two maps of a server; a race it can't read counts as online. F6 works everywhere as before. Log: photo: online (race ...): auto photo mode off, F6 still works. Test: tmvs_photoautotest.
- Short stalls on the game's thread from read-backs: the sea level measured on the water material (4 times a second on maps whose sea the game reports no height for), the minimap's copy of its picture (every few seconds while it fills) and the once-per-map HDR numbers in the log each read a render target back right away, which made the CPU wait for the GPU's whole frame so far. They are now copied behind the GPU's work and read a frame or two later; the HDR numbers are counted on a thread of their own.
